findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded as plaintext Lambda environment variables in the Terraform configuration. These credentials are committed to version control, stored in Terraform state, and visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration permissions.

The Lambda function's environment variables contain secrets but no kms_key_arn is specified, so they are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in plaintext via the console/API by any principal with function read permissions.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.
No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so unsigned or tampered deployment packages can be deployed to the function without integrity verification.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group egress controls, which would allow exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the code were compromised.
